planting.note: Seedless triploid; start indoors or transplant after soil is thoroughly warm, and plant alongside a seeded pollenizer watermelon for fruit set. Fascination carries intermediate resistance to Fusarium wilt race 1 and anthracnose race 1, and holds and ships well, an advantage for gardeners who store melons rather than eating them immediately.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm; Fascination is a seedless triploid watermelon hybrid bred with intermediate resistance to Fusarium wilt race 1 and anthracnose race 1, two diseases that can build up quickly in warm, humid Gulf Coast soil. Because triploid seedless varieties produce little viable pollen of their own, plant a seeded pollenizer variety nearby to ensure good fruit set. It produces large, crisp, sweet red-fleshed fruit with excellent post-harvest holding quality, staying in good eating condition longer after picking than many other seedless types. Harvest when the ground spot beneath the fruit turns from white to creamy yellow and the nearest tendril has dried and browned.
sources: seed catalog reference (Stokes Seeds, Rupp Seeds, Osborne Seed Company)

planting.note: Seedless triploid; start indoors or transplant after soil is thoroughly warm, and plant alongside a seeded pollenizer watermelon for fruit set. Exclamation carries intermediate resistance to Fusarium wilt race 1 and anthracnose race 1, and was bred to reduce hollow heart, a common quality defect in large seedless melons grown in Southern heat.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm; Exclamation is a full-season seedless watermelon hybrid bred with intermediate resistance to Fusarium wilt race 1 and anthracnose race 1, along with reduced tendency toward hollow heart, a cracking defect that can hollow out the center of large seedless melons grown under Southern heat stress. Because triploid seedless varieties need a seeded pollenizer nearby for fruit set, plant a compatible pollenizer variety in the same bed. It produces large, blocky, crimson-fleshed fruit with excellent sweetness and firm texture. Harvest when the ground spot beneath the fruit turns from white to creamy yellow and the nearest tendril has dried and browned.
sources: seed catalog reference (Rupp Seeds, Stokes Seeds)

planting.note: Start indoors or transplant after soil is thoroughly warm; Sangria carries resistance to anthracnose and Fusarium wilt and produces the classic large, oblong shipping-type melon long grown across Southern watermelon country.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm; Sangria is a widely grown seeded watermelon hybrid bred with resistance to anthracnose and Fusarium wilt, giving it reliable performance in the hot, humid disease pressure typical of a Gulf South summer. It produces large, oblong, dark green-striped fruit in the classic 20-24 pound shipping-melon range, with firm, deep red, sweet flesh that holds up well to handling and short-term storage. The vigorous vines set fruit dependably over a long harvest window. Harvest when the ground spot beneath the fruit turns from white to creamy yellow and the nearest tendril has dried and browned.
sources: seed catalog reference (Harris Seeds, Rupp Seeds, Territorial Seed)

planting.note: Seedless triploid; start indoors or transplant after soil is thoroughly warm, and plant alongside a seeded pollenizer watermelon for fruit set. Affirmed is part of a modern seedless watermelon series bred for reliable yields in warm Southern production regions.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm; Affirmed is a seedless triploid watermelon hybrid bred as part of a modern commercial series developed for consistent, high-count yields under Southern growing conditions. Because triploid seedless varieties produce little viable pollen, plant a seeded pollenizer variety nearby to ensure good fruit set on the vines. It produces medium to large, crisp, sweet, deep red-fleshed fruit with the classic dark green striping. Harvest when the ground spot beneath the fruit turns from white to creamy yellow and the nearest tendril has dried and browned, and handle seedless melons gently since their rinds tend to be slightly thinner than seeded types.
sources: trade press reference (Growing Produce — Sakata watermelon variety coverage)

common_name: Cal Sweet Bush Watermelon (Compact Bush-Habit AAS Winner)

planting.note: Start indoors or transplant after soil is thoroughly warm; Cal Sweet Bush is a 2019 All-America Selections winner with a true short-internode bush habit, growing on vines only 14-18 inches long rather than sprawling 8-10 feet like standard watermelon, making it ideal for small Gulf Coast raised beds and containers.

directions: Transplant into warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm; Cal Sweet Bush is a genuine dwarf-vine watermelon, growing on compact 14-18 inch vines instead of the sprawling 8-10 foot vines of standard varieties, so it fits in a small raised bed or even a large container without taking over the garden. It still produces good-sized, 8-10 pound, round melons with sweet red flesh and the classic striped rind. Because the compact vines carry fewer leaves to shade developing fruit, keep an eye on ripening melons in intense heat to prevent sunscald. Harvest when the ground spot beneath the fruit turns from white to creamy yellow and the nearest tendril has dried and browned.
sources: All-America Selections — Cal Sweet Bush watermelon AAS winner 2019
